text:
lee: Heads up — encountered two weird things in the onboarding sample app when running cross-SDK checks:

1) Python embeddings come back length 1024, Java returns 1023 for same input.
2) Rerank endpoint in Java sample returns scores as strings ("0.9123") while Python returns numbers (0.9123).

lee: Quick repro: both SDKs call batching helper (AutoBatcher) with same batchOptions and model rdw-embed-large.

lee: Python snippet:
```py
res = client.embeddings.create(model='rdw-embed-large', input='query text')
print(len(res.data[0].embedding)) # 1024
rr = client.rerank.create(model='rdw-rank-v1', inputs=[...])
print(type(rr.data[0].score)) # <class 'float'>
```

lee: Java snippet:
```java
var res = client.embeddings().create(new EmbeddingsRequest("rdw-embed-large", List.of("query text")));
System.out.println(res.getData().get(0).getEmbedding().size()); // 1023
var rr = client.rerank().create(req);
System.out.println(rr.getData().get(0).getScore().getClass()); // java.lang.String
```

ankit: Ugh. My bet: packing/padding + JSON marshalling differences. Maybe Java SDK is trimming trailing zeros from float array when converting to JSON (or the server returns full vector but Java unmarshal loses one). The rerank-as-string smells like an earlier wire-format change where score was sent as string for precision safety and some SDKs parse it to float, some don't.

maya: We rolled a small change last week to the auth middleware that reconstructs request body from buffered parts on token refresh. If padding was appended as a sentinel zero it might be lost when body is rebuilt. I saw a flaky test in CI about embedding lengths failing in Java.

lee: Here's trimmed debug from local run:
```
[2026-03-22T15:00:01Z] batcher: batch size 4 pad=1 -> desired_len=1024
[2026-03-22T15:00:01Z] send id=req-77 headers: Authorization: Bearer xxxx
[2026-03-22T15:00:01Z] auth: 401, refreshing token
[2026-03-22T15:00:01Z] retry: rebuild body from buffer (pad metadata omitted)
[2026-03-22T15:00:01Z] response: embedding_len=1023
[2026-03-22T15:00:01Z] rerank: score serialized as "0.9123"
```

ankit: That log nails it. If pad metadata is in the high-level batch object and not part of the raw buffer, the retry path could drop it. Different SDKs store pad data differently; Java probably relied on buffer-only pads.

emily: For rerank-as-string, we have a transitional wire contract where some models return score as string to avoid scientific notation drift. The SDKs need to normalise on receive. Python has a postprocess that casts numeric-like strings to floats; Java's parser currently leaves them as strings.

lee: OK — immediate workaround instructions I pushed to the onboarding README: set env SDK_STRICT_PAD=1 to force no-retry path on auth expiry or set batcher.padToMultiple = true so the helper pads at creation time (avoids reconstruct path). Also for rerank: add a small conv layer in Java sample: if score instanceof String -> Double.parseDouble((String)score).

maya: I'll open two GH issues: one for pad persistence on retry across SDKs, one for rerank response normalization. Please add minimal repro traces.

ci-bot: Created issue #4872 in repo sdk-java: "persist batch pad metadata across auth retries" by maya
repo-bot: Created issue #4873 in repo sdk-core: "normalize rerank score types across SDKs" by emily

ankit: I'll own the Java pad fix. Plan: persist a small metadata map in the request context that includes padCount and originalDesiredLen. Ensure auth retry uses requestContext.getMetadata() not raw buffer. Add unit and integration tests. Also add a debug env: SDK_DEBUG_PAD=1 to log pad actions.

emily: I'll add a tiny post-process step in sdk-core: when parsing rerank responses, coerce numeric-like strings into floats. Add a flag SDK_RERANK_STRICT=true to fail on non-numeric if customers want strict typing.

lee: Test script idea to catch both issues (will add to sampleapp CI):
```bash
# compare across SDKs
node scripts/get_embed.js > node.json
python scripts/get_embed.py > py.json
java -jar samples/java-get-embed.jar > java.json
NODE_LEN=$(jq .data[0].embedding | jq length < node.json)
PY_LEN=$(jq .data[0].embedding | jq length < py.json)
JAVA_LEN=$(jq .data[0].embedding | jq length < java.json)
if [ "$NODE_LEN" -ne "$PY_LEN" ] || [ "$NODE_LEN" -ne "$JAVA_LEN" ]; then
  echo "embed dim mismatch: node=$NODE_LEN py=$PY_LEN java=$JAVA_LEN"; exit 2
fi
# rerank type check
JAVASCORE=$(jq .data[0].score < java.json)
PYTHONSCORE=$(jq .data[0].score < py.json)
if echo "$JAVASCORE" | grep -q '"'; then
  echo "java rerank score serialized as string"; exit 3
fi
```

maya: I'll add to the internal release notes and flag customers who touched embed batchers in last 7 days.

ankit: PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-java/pull/312 — persists pad metadata, adds tests.

emily: PR opened in sdk-core: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-core/pull/410 — rerank normalization + feature flag.

lee: Thanks team. Once CI passes on both we'll cut a patch release and update sampleapp. If anyone hits a parity issue after patch, please paste request id from logs and ping this thread.

maya: Also note: for customers on Dedicated, routing proxies already keep pad metadata. This is mainly hitting self-hosted sampleapps or edge SDKs that do request reconstruction.

lee: cool. tagging: @ankit @emily @maya. I verified locally after toggling SDK_STRICT_PAD=1 and Java now returns 1024. Will run full CI tomorrow. :rocket:
